findings.title: The commit shadow-domain control can never pass, because currentness integrity() renders format_type() under the pg_temp type shadows
findings.claim:
The TC3-shadow-commit session creates pg_temp jsonb, text, uuid and timestamptz domains, then expects a successful commit with five effects.

On the way, the commit calls the accepted currentness read_strict_authority and resolve_scope, and each performs integrity(). integrity() compares install-time digests built from pg_catalog.format_type() with:
- the source-column descriptor seal;
- the guard trigger comments;
- the schema fingerprint.

format_type() qualifies any type that is not visible. pg_temp is searched first and now holds same-named types, so pg_catalog.text, uuid and jsonb render as 'pg_catalog.text' and so on (timestamptz is special-cased). The commit therefore raises 55000 before any write. startupSql rejects, the control fails at the third loop iteration, and every later intake verifier control is skipped.

The admin and replay controls are unaffected because they make no currentness calls. TC-21 (the NULL descriptor seal) hides all of this today. Doc 87 did not identify it, and r4 neither handles nor discloses it. Reasoned, NOT RUN.

findings.title: 'Differently schemed frames refuse' overstates the schema check
findings.claim:
In PostgreSQL 17, the CONTEXT line for a SQL function carries only the unqualified proname. A PL/pgSQL fn_signature is unqualified whenever the function was visible at compile time.

So caller.schema==='' accepts a same-named function in any schema, and the 'canonical frame schema differs' check binds only PL/pgSQL frames rendered with a non-public schema.

This is not exploitable in this harness: every intake-to-canonical and canonical-to-canonical call is public-qualified, and pg_temp functions are never resolved unqualified. But the comment claims more than the check enforces.
findings.evidence: mjs:1178-1179@38915cf4 (comment 'Unknown or differently schemed frames refuse'); mjs:1199-1202 and :1265 (schema '' accepted). Fixture :1295 tests only a quoted-schema SQL name, which PostgreSQL never renders.
findings.fix: Reword the comment and records to 'canonical names are exact; schema is enforced only where PostgreSQL renders it'. Optionally require kind==='sql' or 'plpgsql' per allowlisted name.

verdicts.note:
CONFIRMED.

The mechanism:
- integrity() runs with search_path='' (currentness:598-599), so the effective type path is [pg_temp_N, pg_catalog].
- With pg_temp.text, pg_temp.uuid and pg_temp.jsonb present, TypeIsVisible() is false for the pg_catalog types, so pg_catalog.format_type renders 'pg_catalog.text' and so on. timestamptz is special-cased and stays unqualified.
- These renderings feed the descriptor digest (:615-624), the guard trigger comments (:700-704) and the schema fingerprint (:62, :75, :709-712).
- read_strict_authority performs integrity() first (:1060), and the commit calls it on every new key at intake.sql:597, after replay returns null.
- So once the descriptor is bound, the shadow commit refuses with 55000. The loop at mjs:1321-1336 then throws at kind='commit', and every control after mjs:873 is skipped.
- Today TC-21 masks it, because integrity() raises 'not yet bound' at :602.

Evidence corrections to the lens:
- resolve_scope does not call integrity(); :1229 is guard_source_write.
- The corroborating currentness control (currentness_local.mjs:1546-1558) fails at guard_source_write's 'protected source columns drift', not at integrity()'s descriptor check. The mechanism is the same.

On the fix: no shadow of text, uuid or jsonb can ever reach the commit's intake body after :597, because the accepted currentness gate fails closed by design. So a named limit is needed under either option.

A possible partial recovery, reasoned and NOT RUN: a timestamptz-only commit shadow session. format_type special-cases TIMESTAMPTZOID, so the integrity renderings should not change, and the commit body's timestamptz resolution could then be dynamically observed.
